headline: Japan to provide $317m loan to Bangladesh; Dhaka and Tokyo upgrade BIG-B initiative
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi held a high-level bilateral meeting in Tokyo to strengthen economic ties and democratic values.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi held a high-level bilateral summit in Tokyo following an official invitation from the Japanese leader.

The meeting focused on elevating the friendly relations between the two nations to new heights, with PM Takaichi congratulating PM Tarique Rahman on his ascent to power through a historic democratic general election.
A major highlight was the upgrade of the 'Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt' (BIG-B) into a new strategic cooperation initiative called 'Sharing Prosperity BIG-B'.
Japan has committed to providing a $317 million loan to Bangladesh to bolster economic resilience and energy security.
PM Takaichi emphasized that Bangladesh's economy is crucial for Japan due to its strategic location as a junction between South and Southeast Asia and its large, youthful population.
Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to working together to implement a 'Free and Open Indo-Pacific' (FOIP) region.
PM Tarique Rahman expressed gratitude for Japan's long-standing support and friendship, noting Japan's early recognition of Bangladesh's independence.
The summit concluded with a joint statement outlining a historic roadmap for the two countries to move forward together with strength and prosperity.
caption:
Japan provides $317m loan to Bangladesh as Dhaka and Tokyo upgrade their strategic economic partnership.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi held a high-level bilateral summit in Tokyo following an official invitation from the Japanese leader.

The meeting focused on elevating the friendly relations between the two nations to new heights, with PM Takaichi congratulating PM Tarique Rahman on his ascent to power through a historic democratic general election.

A major highlight was the upgrade of the 'Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt' (BIG-B) into a new strategic cooperation initiative called 'Sharing Prosperity BIG-B'.

Japan has committed to providing a $317 million loan to Bangladesh to bolster economic resilience and energy security.

PM Takaichi emphasized that Bangladesh's economy is crucial for Japan due to its strategic location as a junction between South and Southeast Asia and its large, youthful population.

Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to working together to implement a 'Free and Open Indo-Pacific' (FOIP) region.

PM Tarique Rahman expressed gratitude for Japan's long-standing support and friendship, noting Japan's early recognition of Bangladesh's independence.

The summit concluded with a joint statement outlining a historic roadmap for the two countries to move forward together with strength and prosperity.

headline_marked: Home Minister: [[IGP’s ‘crossfire’ remarks do not reflect govt position]]
headline: Home Minister: IGP’s ‘crossfire’ remarks do not reflect govt position
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed clarifies that the government is firmly opposed to extrajudicial killings and custodial deaths.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the police chief's comments regarding conducting 'crossfire' with government permission do not represent the government's official stance.
The Home Minister emphasized that the government is firmly opposed to extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, and custodial deaths, committing to the rule of law.
The controversy began when Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir stated at a program in Dhaka's Chawkbazar that police would conduct 'crossfire' if the government allowed it.
Police Headquarters later clarified that the IGP did not intend to endorse extrajudicial killings, but was referring to firm action against criminals within the law.
The Bangladesh Police Service Association defended the IGP, calling his remarks a 'timely call' for the enforcement of the law and the right of private defense.
Under Articles 31 and 32 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, no person can be deprived of life except in accordance with the law, making government permission for extrajudicial killings illegal.
Data from Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK) shows that 2,957 people were killed in alleged crossfires or gunfights involving law enforcement agencies between 2004 and September 2026.
caption:
Can the government permit 'crossfire'? The Home Minister says no, distancing the government from the IGP's controversial remarks.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the police chief's comments regarding conducting 'crossfire' with government permission do not represent the government's official stance.

The Home Minister emphasized that the government is firmly opposed to extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, and custodial deaths, committing to the rule of law.

The controversy began when Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir stated at a program in Dhaka's Chawkbazar that police would conduct 'crossfire' if the government allowed it.

Police Headquarters later clarified that the IGP did not intend to endorse extrajudicial killings, but was referring to firm action against criminals within the law.

The Bangladesh Police Service Association defended the IGP, calling his remarks a 'timely call' for the enforcement of the law and the right of private defense.

Under Articles 31 and 32 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, no person can be deprived of life except in accordance with the law, making government permission for extrajudicial killings illegal.

Data from Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK) shows that 2,957 people were killed in alleged crossfires or gunfights involving law enforcement agencies between 2004 and September 2026.
